name: Lamandau, 'bahasa Lamandau'
confidence_why: The only description of a Lamandau variety, Nanang et al. 1992, calls word stress non-phonemic and splits its cues, with pitch on the open initial syllable but length on the second syllable, while Smith 2017 expects word-final stress across the Malayic Dayak languages, so no placement can be defended.

catalog_quote: 3.6 Aspek Suprasegmental. Dalam data yang ada aspek suprasegmental dalam bahasa Lamandau tidak fonemis. Pembicaraan mengenainya hanya mencakup tekanan kata saja. Tekanan kata yang dibicarakan meliputi tinggi nada dan rentang waktu. Intensitas tidak dibicarakan. 3.6.1 Tinggi Nada. Tinggi nada dalam bahasa Lamandau terdapat pada suku awal terbuka, baik yang terdiri atas sebuah fonem maupun lebih. Contoh: [ʔi'na] 'ibu' [ʔi'na] 'dia' [ʔu'nun] 'isap' [ta'nUʔ] 'tanduk' [ko'cIt̚] 'kecil'. Tinggi nada ini sering bervariasi dengan penggandaan konsonan yang terletak setelah suku yang bertekanan itu. Contoh: [ʔi'na] – [ʔinʔna] 'ibu' [ʔi'na] – [ʔinʔna] 'dia' [ʔu'nun] – [ʔunʔnun] 'isap' [na'wa] – [nawʔwa] 'mulut' [ta'nUʔ] – [tanʔnUʔ] 'tanduk'. 3.6.2 Rentang Waktu. Dalam bahasa Lamandau rentang waktu dalam pengucapan kata terjadi pada kata yang terdiri atas dua buah suku. Suku kedua terbuka. Rentang waktu pada suku kedua lebih panjang daripada rentang waktu suku pertama. Contoh: [tobu] 'tebu' [tanti] 'hadang' [kita] 'kita' [jora] 'jora' [bini] 'istri'.

new_statements.translation: In the available data the suprasegmental aspect of Lamandau is not phonemic. Its discussion covers word stress only. The word stress discussed comprises pitch height and duration. ... High pitch in Lamandau occurs on an open initial syllable, whether it consists of one phoneme or more. Examples: [?i'na] 'mother' ... [ta'nU?] 'horn', [ko'cIt] 'small'. This high pitch often alternates with gemination of the consonant located after that stressed syllable. Examples: [?i'na] ~ [?in?na] 'mother' ... In Lamandau, duration in the pronunciation of words applies to words of two syllables where the second syllable is open: the duration of the second syllable is longer than that of the first. Examples: [tobu] 'sugarcane' ... [bini] 'wife'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is not contrastive. The authors decompose 'word stress' into pitch and duration: the high-pitch (and, in their words, 'stressed') syllable is the open initial syllable, optionally followed by a geminated consonant; but in disyllables the open final syllable is the longer one. All examples are disyllabic, so the pitch-prominent syllable is both initial and penultimate; no rule is given for longer words. Net: pitch prominence on the first/penultimate syllable of disyllables with final lengthening -- placement for the word class as a whole is left unclear.
new_statements.exceptions: High pitch stated only for OPEN initial syllables; duration effect stated only for disyllables with an open second syllable; intensity explicitly not discussed.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation-form words (elicited from speakers of Seituat, Tanjung Beringin, Penopa, Tapinbini); word-level 'tekanan kata'; no phrase-level discussion.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes 'bahasa Lamandau' (= Dayak Tomun of the Lamandau river; fieldwork villages Seituat, Tanjung Beringin, Penopa, Tapinbini, Kec. Lamandau, then Kab. Kotawaringin Barat, Kalimantan Tengah), which Glottolog 5.1 lists as the dialect Lamandau [lama1276] under Malayic Dayak mala1480. The other two Glottolog-listed sketches cover Kayung/Ketapang Malay [kayu1242] (Ahadi et al. 1998) and Krio Dayak of Ketapang (Mecer et al. 1992); both are silent on stress placement. sources.note: sec. 3.6 pp.169-170: suprasegmentals not phonemic; 'tekanan kata' treated as pitch height + duration: high pitch on the open initial syllable (all examples disyllabic: [?i'na] 'ibu', [ta'nU?] 'tanduk', [ko'cIt] 'kecil'), often with gemination of the consonant after 'the stressed syllable' ([?in?na]); in disyllables the open second syllable is longer than the first ([tobu], [bini]). Intensity not discussed.
